entities.summary:
Universal Pictures, founded in 1912 by Carl Laemmle as one of Hollywood's original studios, is the world's oldest and one of the highest-grossing film studios — producing Jaws (1975), E.T. (1982), Jurassic Park (1993), the Fast & Furious franchise ($7+ billion), the Despicable Me franchise ($3.7+ billion), and the Universal Classic Monsters (Dracula, Frankenstein, The Mummy) that defined horror cinema's golden age. Universal's history encompasses 110+ years of American cinema, from silent nickelodeon to streaming, and the Jurassic World Evolution theme park business.

Carl Laemmle's Universal Film Manufacturing Company opened Universal City (1915) — Hollywood's first purpose-built studio with public tours that continue today — establishing the studio tour model. Universal's 1931-1936 Classic Monsters cycle (Dracula with Bela Lugosi, Frankenstein with Boris Karloff, The Mummy, The Wolf Man) created the horror genre's foundational archetypes. Steven Spielberg's Jaws (1975, $476 million worldwide on $9 million budget, Universal) invented the summer blockbuster model that still governs studio economics.

Universal's NBCUniversal acquisition by Comcast (2011, $30 billion) gave it cable television assets alongside film. The Jurassic World and Fast & Furious franchises — each exceeding $7 billion worldwide — demonstrated Universal's 21st-century franchise ability. Universal's theme park business (Universal Studios Hollywood, Universal Orlando, Universal Japan) generates $5+ billion annually, with Jurassic World attractions using the film brand to create physical entertainment. Peacock streaming (launched 2020) added Universal's content to the streaming wars.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Universal Pictures' 110-year history — from Laemmle's nickelodeon era through Classic Monsters to Jaws's summer blockbuster invention to Jurassic World's theme park empire — spans the entire arc of American cinema, making Universal the studio whose history most completely encodes Hollywood's evolution.
